chunks: From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, when Allah loves a servant, He sends an angel to him and says: 'Make him ill and intensify the affliction upon him; and whenever he is relieved of one trial, afflict him with something more severe than it, and be hard on him until he remembers Me, for I long to hear his supplication. And when He despises a servant, He appoints an angel to him and says: 'Keep him healthy and provide for him so that he may not remember Me, for I do not wish to hear his voice.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah send trials to those He loves?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Mumin* elucidates the dialectic of divine love and displeasure through the mechanism of affliction (*balā'*) and ease (*in'isām*). It highlights the Shia scholarly view that trials are not merely punishments but a means of spiritual refinement, where Allah desires the intimate connection of hearing the servant's supplication, whereas ease can lead to heedlessness (*ghaflah*).

en.muhajir-b-ali: 44. It is narrated that Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) said:

Verily, when Allah loves a person, He sends him an angel saying, 'Strike him with disease and intensify afflictions on him; and every time he is relieved of one trial, afflict with another that is more severe, and be hard on him - until he starts remembering Me, for I long to hear his supplications and his voice calling out to Me' And when He despises a person, He appoints him an angel and says, 'Keep him healthy and provide for him that he may not remember Me; for I do not wish to hear his voice.'
